T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. # agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot: ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **Post-action waits** observe the ref's original process. Window-owned refs stay pinned to their original window, including refs captured from a sheet, alert, popover, focused view, or Linux menu. macOS application menus keep their application-owned surface and need no document window. The wait reads the whole pinned window, so overlay selectors share its scope. [Wait scope and results](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/configuration#post-action-wait-flags) describe the selector limits. - `type`, `set-value`, and `clipboard-set` accept `--stdin` for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start). ## How it works

by people and the agents working alongside them. **Currently in Beta** · Built on [React 19+](https://react.dev) and [StyleX](https://stylexjs.com) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@astryxdesign/core?label=npm&color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@astryxdesign/core) [![license MIT](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@astryxdesign/core?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-astryx.atmeta.com-6741d9?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com) [![Storybook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Storybook-live-ff4785?logo=storybook&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/) [![Sandbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox-playground-A9792B)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/) **[Docs](https://astryx.atmeta.com)** · **[Storybook](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/)** · **[Sandbox](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/)** · **[Contributing](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing)** · **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)**
## Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. **What makes Astryx different:** - **Open internals.** Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. - **No styling lock-in.** Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with `className` using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. - **Customize without wrapping.** A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. - **Built for people and agents.** The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. ## Getting Started Astryx requires **React 19** or later (`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies of `@astryxdesign/core`). Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: ```bash # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli ``` Then finish setup with `init`, once, before you write UI. It asks no questions, prints the getting-started steps (styles, theme), and saves the Astryx guide to `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` so you and your agents build with Astryx instead of guessing: ```bash npx @astryxdesign/cli init # or: pnpm exec astryx init / yarn astryx init ``` You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so `astryx` works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version: ```bash npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli ``` Project install, global install, or both? `astryx docs global/project-global-or-both` compares them (both is recommended), and `astryx docs global` explains how global mode works. The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the **[@astryxdesign/core README](packages/core/README.md#quick-start)** for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your `package.json`: ```json "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } ``` Then use it as `npm run astryx -- component --list`. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. ## Packages | Package | Description | README | | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------

# Auto Ontology

[![#1 on the BEAVER leaderboard](https://img.shields.io/badge/BEAVER_leaderboard-%231-76b900)](https://beaverbench.github.io/#leaderboard)
[![#2 on the BIRD-Interact leaderboard](https://img.shields.io/badge/BIRD--Interact_leaderboard-%232-76b900)](https://bird-interact.github.io/)

Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need context to answer accurately: what each business concept means, where it lives, how it connects, how to calculate it, where it comes from, and whether to trust it. An ontology holds that context: a shared, governed map from the concepts people ask about to the data behind them. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that ontology automatically from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own, and [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/) keeps it portable.

It enables developers to:

- **Discover:** generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs.
- **Ground:** give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems.
- **Validate:** test a draft with real questions before experts certify it; check generated queries against the catalog and the definitions retrieval surfaced; return the SQL and steps with every answer.
- **Expose:** serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.
- **Learn:** fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with use.

An ontology matters most when:

- questions are varied, open-ended, and ambiguous;
- data spans many disparate sources with overlapping or conflicting
  definitions;
- meanings must be reused and governed across runs, teams, and agents;
- the model or its context budget can't hold the full documentation;
- users ask in business terms and need routing to the right source and grain.

With one well-modeled source and a fixed set of questions, direct SQL may be
enough.

## Quickstart

This runs Auto Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers,
Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2,
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from
[build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com).

1. Clone the repository and create `.env`:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

   Then set these values in `.env`:

   ```dotenv
   DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-...
   AUTH_SECRET=<a long random string, e.g. from openssl rand -base64 32>
   APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
   POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<a new password>
   CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:<the same password>@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters
   AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<a new password>
   PGADMIN_PASSWORD=<a new password>
   ```

   Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace
   each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API
   key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or
   delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`.

2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in
   auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set:

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d --wait postgres
   git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval
   (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \
     POSTGRES_PASSWORD='<the same password>' \
     uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop)
   ```

3. Build and start the rest of the stack:

   ```bash

Диаграммы поддерживают 51 тип, не используют тени и не полагаются на Mermaid, что делает их визуально чистыми и легко встраиваемыми в веб‑страницы.

Кроме генерации, инструмент умеет импортировать схемы из Drawio, Mermaid, Excalidraw и PlantUML и экспортировать их в PNG или SVG, что упрощает миграцию существующих визуализаций.

Он объединяет набор высококлассных инструментов: дизассемблер, ассемблер, декомпилятор, графический просмотр кода и скриптовый движок, позволяя исследовать бинарные файлы на Windows, macOS и Linux. Платформа поддерживает сотни наборов инструкций и форматов исполняемых файлов, а также может работать в интерактивном режиме или в полностью автоматизированных пайплайнах, что упрощает масштабирование и совместную работу над сложными задачами SRE.

Пользователи могут расширять функциональность Ghidra, пиша собственные скрипты и плагины на Java или Python через плагин GhidraDev для Eclipse или интеграцию с Visual Studio Code. Это делает возможным автоматизацию повторяющихся анализов, добавление новых процессорных модулей или создание специализированных визуализаций. Пример применения: аналитик по кибербезопасности получает подозрительный образец вредоносного кода, запускает автоматический скрипт, который декомпилирует функции, строит граф вызовов и сразу же экспортирует результаты в отчёт, экономя часы ручного исследования.

Для работы требуется 64‑разрядный JDK 25 и, в случае сборки из исходников, Gradle 9.1+, Python 3.9‑3.15, а также компиляторы GCC/Clang (Linux/macOS) или Visual Studio 2017+ (Windows). В официальных релизах уже включён готовый набор зависимостей, но сборка из кода требует наличия интернета для загрузки дополнительных библиотек. Важно учитывать, что в некоторых версиях обнаружены уязвимости, о чём предупреждает раздел Security Warning, поэтому перед использованием следует ознакомиться с соответствующими advisory.

latest.readme_excerpt: # Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the [National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components and/or scripts using Java or Python. In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential vulnerabilities in networks and systems. For issues building, please check the [Known Issues][known-issues] section for possible solutions. ## Develop ### User Scripts and Extensions Ghidra installations support users writing custom scripts and extensions via the *GhidraDev* plugin for Eclipse. # Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. Requires Node.js 22 or later. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color).

📐 CSS Layout

Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid, modern color spaces like oklch, text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming).

⚡ Performance

Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield).

📝 Forms & UI

Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields).

После установки через скрипт, npm, Homebrew или другие менеджеры пользователь получает консольный интерфейс, который может выполнять команды, редактировать файлы и запускать bash‑скрипты. Внутри продукта реализованы два основных режима: «build» — полнофункциональный агент с правом изменять код и выполнять любые операции, и «plan» — ограниченный режим, который только читает проект, запрашивает подтверждение перед запуском команд и подходит для изучения чужих репозиториев или планирования изменений. Кроме того, существует суб‑агент «@general», позволяющий выполнять сложные поисковые запросы и многошаговые задачи. Примером применения может быть ситуация, когда разработчик получает новую кодовую базу, переключается в режим «plan», исследует структуру и зависимости, а затем, убедившись в необходимости правок, переключается в «build» и автоматически генерирует или исправляет файлы. Требования к системе минимальны: нужен доступ к интернету для загрузки скрипта и, при использовании «build», права на запись в каталог проекта; в случае desktop‑версии приложение ставится в домашний каталог ~/.opencode/bin. Ограничения включают необходимость удаления устаревших версий (< 0.1.x) перед установкой и то, что «plan» по умолчанию запрещает изменения, требуя явного согласия пользователя.

Claude Code Game Studios

Describe a game. Claude Code asks a few questions, writes a one-page brief, and builds a playable browser game from it.
Then you change it, grow it and finish it, one step at a time.

--- ## Make me a game Open Claude Code in a copy of this repository and say what you want: ``` /prototype a fishing game where the rare fish only bite at dusk ``` 1. **A few questions.** One round, picked from the genre: the choices that shape the game, how it should feel, how it looks, how hard it is, the goal. Each has a usual answer, so "you pick" works. A vague idea ("a racing game") gets two or three one-line pitches to choose from first. 2. **A one-page brief.** `design/game-brief.md`: your words kept as you typed them, the look, the first minute, the challenge, the features and what is left for later. You read it and say Build it, or change something first. 3. **A first build.** A browser game in `prototypes//` that opens with a double-click: every figure drawn, no emoji art, no copy of another game, and not trivially easy. Your session builds it at its own effort ("build it at medium" is cheaper and thinner). 4. **Checked before you get it.** A few scripted key presses in a headless browser show it opens with no errors and responds; text that is too small, overlapping or off screen and screens that freeze are fixed in one round; and every line of the brief is marked built, missing or broken from the screenshots and the code, or not assessed when it could not be checked. Your play is the real test: the handover card says what passed, what is still broken and what was guessed, and ends "Not yet played by a person". Then it is yours to play. After that: - **Change it by asking.** Each change is checked against what you said to keep and to avoid, and each one you accept is a checkpoint you can go back to. Ask to tune it and it gains a tweak panel with a slider for every value. - **Share it.** A clean copy without the panel and the working files, ready for itch.io or a link. - **Grow it.** When you like it, it becomes a real web project (Vite and TypeScript, its values in data files, tests and a build), and you add to it one feature a sitting: say the next feature, and it is built, checked and committed. After every feature the same seeded run is played again and any change is shown to you. Stories (`/create-stories`, `/dev-story`, `/story-done`) only when you ask for them. - **Finish it.** `/cut` proposes what to cut and a polish list, and a date when the game is to sell. Already have a browser game? `/prototype --from ` brings a copy in as it is, so it can be changed and grown the same way. ## What it has been shown to do - **The first build.** In a blind comparison on three game ideas, the brief made from its questions was picked over a hand-written brief all three times. All six games built from the two kinds of brief were ones the tester said they would build on, so on the games themselves the two kinds of brief tied. - **Growing.** One game was grown from its first build through six stories into a game the tester would keep building. That is one game, not yet a pattern. - **Not yet shown:** the engine route (Godot, Unity, Unreal) and deepening one system with a design document. Both are built and pass the framework's own checks, but neither has had a test like the two above. The games themselves are deliberately **not** shipped here: this is a template you clone to start your own project, and somebody else's game in your repo is clutter, not evidence. --- ## Table of Contents - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [Engines](#engines) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Upgrading](#upgrading) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [Hooks, Permissions and Rules](#hooks-permissions-and-rules) - [Studio Mode](#studio-mode) - [Design Philosophy](#design-philosophy) - [Customization](#customization) - [Platform Support](#platform-support) - [Community](#community) - [Supporting This Project](#supporting-this-project) - [License](#license) --- ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - [Git](https://git-scm.

> **Note:** This repository contains Anthropic's implementation of skills for Claude. For information about the Agent Skills standard, see [agentskills.io](http://agentskills.io).

[![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/anthropics/skills)](https://skills.sh/anthropics/skills)

# Skills
Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.

For more information, check out:
- [What are skills?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills)
- [Using skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-using-skills-in-claude)
- [How to create custom skills](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-creating-custom-skills)
- [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](https://anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)

# About This Repository

This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. These skills range from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows (communications, branding, etc.).

Each skill is self-contained in its own folder with a `SKILL.md` file containing the instructions and metadata that Claude uses. Browse through these skills to get inspiration for your own skills or to understand different patterns and approaches.

Many skills in this repo are open source (Apache 2.0). We've also included the document creation & editing skills that power [Claude's document capabilities](https://www.anthropic.com/news/create-files) under the hood in the [`skills/docx`](./skills/docx), [`skills/pdf`](./skills/pdf), [`skills/pptx`](./skills/pptx), and [`skills/xlsx`](./skills/xlsx) subfolders. These are also open source (Apache 2.0), and we wanted to share them with developers as a reference for more complex skills that are actively used in a production AI application.

## Disclaimer

**These skills are provided for demonstration and educational purposes only.** While some of these capabilities may be available in Claude, the implementations and behaviors you receive from Claude may differ from what is shown in these skills. These skills are meant to illustrate patterns and possibilities. Always test skills thoroughly in your own environment before relying on them for critical tasks.

# Skill Sets
- [./skills](./skills): Skill examples for Creative & Design, Development & Technical, Enterprise & Communication, and Document Skills
- [./spec](./spec): The Agent Skills specification
- [./template](./template): Skill template

# Try in Claude Code, Claude.ai, and the API

## Claude Code
You can register this repository as a Claude Code Plugin marketplace by running the following command in Claude Code:
```
/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
```

Then, to install a specific set of skills:
1. Select `Browse and install plugins`
2. Select `anthropic-agent-skills`
3. Select `document-skills` or `example-skills`
4. Select `Install now`

Alternatively, directly install either Plugin via:
```
/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
```

After installing the plugin, you can use the skill by just mentioning it. For instance, if you install the `document-skills` plugin from the marketplace, you can ask Claude Code to do something like: "Use the PDF skill to extract the form fields from `path/to/some-file.pdf`"

## Claude.ai

These example skills are all already available to paid plans in Claude.ai. 

To use any skill from this repository or upload custom skills, follow the instructions in [Using skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-using-skills-in-claude#h_a4222fa77b).

## Claude API

You can use Anthropic's pre-built skills, and upload custom skills, via the Claude API. See the [Skills API Quickstart](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/skills-guide#creating-a-skill) for more.

# Creating a Basic Skill

Skills are simple to create - just a folder with a `SKILL.md` file containing YAML frontmatter and instructions. You can use the **template-skill** in this repository as a starting point:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill-name
description: A clear description of what this skill does and when to use it
---

# My Skill Name

[Add your instructions here that Claude will follow when this skill is active]

## Examples
- Example usage 1
- Example usage 2

## Guidelines
- Guideline 1
- Guideline 2
```

# ThinkRail [![JetBrains incubator project](https://jb.gg/badges/incubator-plastic.svg)](https://confluence.jetbrains.com/display/ALL/JetBrains+on+GitHub) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/JetBrains/thinkrail?style=social)](https://star-history.com/#JetBrains/thinkrail&Date) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20the%20chat-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://thinkrail.ai/discord) ThinkRail is an agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it. With Spec-Driven Development support, it learns your project as you work, becoming more capable and helpful over time. We built a rich interface around the `pi` coding agent, isolated work into separate workspaces, and gave the agent durable project knowledge through the spec graph and reusable skills. We are now adding full extension support, so ThinkRail can create the tools it needs based on how you work. **Website:** [thinkrail.ai](https://thinkrail.ai/) · **Blog:** [thinkrail.ai/blog](https://thinkrail.ai/blog/) · **Discord:** [thinkrail.ai/discord](https://thinkrail.ai/discord) ⭐ If you find ThinkRail useful, give it a star. It helps others discover it.

*From the left: An isolated workspace, a work session with an AI agent in that workspace, the code change made by the agent, and the spec tree.* ## Installation ThinkRail ships in two forms: a native desktop installer and the self-contained `thinkrail` CLI. You can install them from out [Landing page](https://thinkrail.ai/#install). For latest version, see the [Releases page](https://github.com/JetBrains/thinkrail/releases). ## What you get - **Isolated workspaces.** Open any git repo as a project and create `git worktree` workspaces from it, each with its own branch and working directory. # Claude Plugins

Anthropic's own plugins for Claude, and the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace for Claude Code.

> **Submitting a plugin?** Submit it at **[claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage)**. Plugins accepted there are served across Claude products. Pull requests to this repository are not monitored.

## What is changing

- **All plugins are now submitted at [claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage)**, and are served across Claude products from there.
- **`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is being phased out for third-party plugins.** It will be reduced over time to Anthropic's own plugins.
- **This repository is the home of Anthropic's own plugins.** Its checks cover the plugin folders here, not the plugins hosted in other repositories.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins added before submissions moved to [claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage), and Anthropic's channel plugins (Discord, fakechat, iMessage and Telegram)

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Third-party plugins

Submit and manage your plugin at [claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage). Do not open a pull request here: pull requests are not monitored, and `marketplace.json` is being reduced to Anthropic's own plugins.

### Anthropic plugins

Plugins in `/plugins` are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation. Every folder there is checked on each pull request, whether or not `marketplace.json` lists it.

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

- To change how a plugin is labeled in the UI, set or update `displayName` instead.
- If a rename is genuinely unavoidable, add an entry to the top-level `renames` map in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` so existing installs auto-migrate:

```json
"renames": {
  "old-name": "new-name"
}
```

The Claude Code plugin loader reads this map and transparently rewrites the old slug to the new one on the user's next sync.

## Skill-bundle plugins

When a plugin's source repository ships skills (`SKILL.md` files) without a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, the marketplace entry can declare the skills directly using `strict: false` and an explicit `skills` array.

```json
{
  "name": "example-bundle",
  "description": "Brief description of the bundled skills.",
  "author": { "name": "Author Name" },
  "category": "development",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk.git",
    "path": "packages/agent-skills",
    "ref": "main",
    "sha": "<commit sha>"
  },
  "strict": false,
  "skills": [
    "./skill-a",
    "./skill-b",
    "./skill-c"
  ],
  "homepage": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk"
}
```

Each path in `skills` is relative to `source.path` and points at a directory containing a `SKILL.md`. Paths can reach deeper than a single level — for example, `["./libA/skill-1", "./libB/skill-2"]` exposes a curated subset across multiple library subdirectories. Each skill is registered as `<plugin-name>:<skill-name>` in Claude Code.

For the underlying schema, see [Strict mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces) in the marketplace documentation.

## License

Please see each linked plugin for the relevant LICENSE file.

## Documentation

For more information on developing Claude Code plugins, see the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins).

Elephant‑Goldfish Model (EGM) — это плагин‑расширение для AI‑ассистентов, позволяющий вести процесс проектирования и последующего ревью программных спецификаций с помощью специализированных под‑агентов. «Elephant» сохраняет контекст проекта и формирует черновик спецификации, а «Goldfish» выступает в роли независимого ревьюера, проверяя черновик и связанные источники без доступа к исходному диалогу, тем самым выявляя скрытые допущения и несоответствия. Пользователь задаёт архитектурные компромиссы, одобряет полученный документ и передаёт его агенту‑разработчику для реализации.

Встроенный workflow поддерживает три ключевых операции: мозговой штурм (генерация требований), черновик (автоматическое составление design_draft.md) и ревью (проверка черновика и сравнение с текущим кодом). Кроме того, команда `/egm-drift-report` сравнивает документы в указанной папке с реальной кодовой базой, выявляя отклонения и предлагая обновить либо документ, либо код. Плагин интегрируется в несколько сред — ChatGPT, Claude, Codex и Antigravity CLI — через простую установку и последующее использование префикса `/egm:` для вызова соответствующих навыков.

Сценарий применения: команда разрабатывает новую функцию веб‑хуков, запускает `/egm-brainstorm` для обсуждения требований, получает от «Elephant» черновик спецификации, затем «Goldfish» проверяет его на полноту и соответствие текущей архитектуре, после чего разработчики получают готовый документ и отчёт о возможных расхождениях с кодом, что ускоряет согласование и снижает риск пропущенных деталей.

Claude SEO

Free, open-source SEO audits inside Claude Code.
Rank higher in Google and get cited by AI search.

Install · Demo · Results · Team · Commands · Pricing · FAQ

**Claude SEO is a free SEO plugin for Claude Code.** Give it any website and it runs a full SEO audit in 10 to 15 minutes, then hands you a clear action plan, sorted by what matters most. It checks everything a good SEO consultant would: - **Technical SEO.** Crawlability, indexing, sitemaps, robots.txt, redirects, page speed and Core Web Vitals. - **Content quality.** E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authority and trust), thin pages and topic coverage. - **Structured data.** Finds, validates and writes Schema.org markup for rich results. - **AI search (GEO).** How likely Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini are to cite your pages. - **Local and e-commerce SEO.** Google Business Profile, reviews, map pack, product pages and international sites. Claude SEO is built from 29 sub-skills and 20 specialist agents, and up to 17 agents work on your site at the same time.
